summary: Re-test of the rate-limit fix (auth `_client_ip` now honours X-Forwarded-For / X-Real-IP). Result: HIGH bug from iteration 2 is FIXED. Auth suite (/app/backend/tests/test_auth_local.py): 14/14 PASSED. Full backend suite: 41/41 PASSED. Specifically `TestRateLimit::test_login_rate_limit_429_on_sixth` now passes — 6th consecutive wrong-password login through the public EXPO_PUBLIC_BACKEND_URL correctly returns 429 (was 400 before the fix). Also verified /api/auth/register + /api/auth/forgot-password still enforce their per-IP buckets correctly; to keep the test suite deterministic in the shared-ingress environment I added unique X-Forwarded-For headers on setup-registrations across independent tests (previous run showed collateral 429s on later tests because now that the real client IP is honoured, all setup calls originate from the same proxy IP within 60s). Rate-limit test itself intentionally pins one X-Forwarded-For for its 6 login attempts. No regressions in trivia backend, admin endpoints, JWT compat, or reset flow. Resend Email + Emergent Push remain MOCKED (placeholder — reset tokens visible in backend.err.log as [EMAIL MOCK]). Bug reported in iteration 2 (rate limiter using request.client.host) has been correctly resolved via the new `_client_ip` helper at server.py:375-384.

minor.issue: passlib 1.7.4 vs bcrypt 4.x still emits 'AttributeError: module bcrypt has no attribute __about__' at startup. Non-blocking (hashing works). Consider pinning bcrypt<4 or upgrading passlib.
Rate limiter is per-process in-memory (resets on backend restart). Adequate for single-worker preview but not for horizontally scaled production. Move to Redis/Mongo TTL for prod.
server.py is ~1358 lines. Consider splitting auth into /app/backend/routers/auth.py (informational, not blocking).

action_items: Nothing blocking. Rate-limit HIGH bug from iteration 2 is verified fixed.
critical_code_review_comments: _client_ip helper (server.py:375-384) correctly parses leftmost X-Forwarded-For then X-Real-IP then falls back to request.client.host — matches iteration-2 recommendation.
Callers updated at server.py:583 (register), :622 (login), :648 (forgot-password) — consistent use of the helper.

SECURITY NOTE (informational): because the helper trusts any X-Forwarded-For, a malicious external client can arbitrarily rotate that header to bypass the per-IP portion of the rate-limit bucket. In this deployment mitigated because the login bucket key is (email, ip) — attackers still hit the per-email limit — but the ('register', ip) and ('forgot', ip) buckets are effectively bypassable by rotating XFF. Not blocking (buckets still exist and Kubernetes ingress is the only real network path in front of uvicorn), but for hardening either (a) trust only the rightmost-untrusted XFF hop, or (b) also key on `email` for register/forgot.
updated_files: /app/backend/tests/test_auth_local.py (added _uniq_ip_headers helper + per-test X-Forwarded-For on setup registrations/forgot calls so independent tests don't share a per-IP bucket; rate-limit test now pins one XFF for its 6 attempts to reliably trip 429)
seed_data_creation: test_auth_* users created via /api/auth/register and cleaned by module-scoped autouse fixture (users + sessions + password_resets). Admin (admin@usfx.bo) untouched.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Rate-limit bug from iteration 2 is verified fixed. Full backend suite green (41/41). Tests in /app/backend/tests/test_auth_local.py now include _uniq_ip_headers() for register/forgot setup so the per-IP buckets don't collide across tests. TestRateLimit intentionally pins one X-Forwarded-For to test the (email, ip) bucket. If new auth tests are added, follow the same pattern.
rca_of_issue: Root cause verified fixed. Original bug: _rate_check used request.client.host, which behind the Kubernetes ingress is the proxy peer IP — often rotating across requests — so per-(email, ip) buckets never accumulated, and 6th failed login returned 400 instead of 429. Fix: new helper `_client_ip` (server.py:375-384) reads leftmost X-Forwarded-For, then X-Real-IP, then falls back to request.client.host. Callers at :583/:622/:648 all use it. Verified end-to-end through the public preview URL: 6th consecutive wrong password → 429.
